source.title: Unveiling Latent Knowledge in Chemistry Language Models through Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: J. Cohen; Alexander Hasson; Sara Tanovic

page_placements.theme: Sparsity settings trade reconstruction against downstream fidelity

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how SAE reconstructions affect the model's loss, which bears on part of V3, but it does not compare that effect with random errors of the same size. It does not test error predictability, context overlap across SAE sizes, or the proposed training-artifact explanation.
record.gate_note: The study reports SAE reconstruction-fidelity sweeps, including model-loss change and fraction of variance explained. The loss result bears on the reconstruction-harm component of V3, but the study does not include the random-error comparison required by that version. The other reported reconstruction metrics do not measure the error behaviors named by V1, V2, V4, V5, or V6.
record.test_reason: The study uses TopK SAEs as a tool to interpret the SMI-TED chemistry model. Its reconstruction metrics (delta loss, fraction of variance explained, SMILES decoding accuracy) only evaluate its own SAE sweep, to pick a configuration. Nothing analyses the SAE error vector: no linear prediction of the error, no per-token error predictability across sizes, no random-error baseline for the loss effect, no error-term ablation in circuits or steering, and no architecture comparison bearing on dark matter. Without a same-norm random-error comparison, delta loss cannot show V3's 'more harmful than random' effect. So no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that SAEs decompose SMI-TED's molecular representations into a more interpretable basis than neurons, with features for substructures, physicochemical descriptors and functional or pharmacological concepts. They add that the SAE gives a more compact toxicity signal and that features are causally steerable by ablation. Stated limitations: a single architecture, manual interpretation, and dependence on the training chemical space. They also say stronger baselines than raw neurons are needed.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains TopK SAEs on pooled molecular representations and evaluates chemical interpretability and reconstruction fidelity. It does not analyze linear predictability or context overlap of SAE errors, and its loss sweep lacks a random-error comparator.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction fidelity changes with sparsity level; the authors report that expansion factor has minimal impact on delta loss at matched sparsity levels.

fits_no_version.finding: On SMI-TED pooled molecular embeddings, TopK SAE fidelity improves with k: FVE is about 0.972 at k=80 and 0.987 at k=160. Delta loss falls exponentially with k, and expansion factor (8x/16x/32x) has minimal impact at matched k. SMILES decoding accuracy from reconstructions is also reported to vary with configuration (Fig. S3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For a chemistry language model's molecule-level embeddings, SAE reconstruction error depends mainly on L0 (k) rather than dictionary size, with diminishing returns in variance explained.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says materials needed for reproduction, including model weights, will be made available at publication.
record.peer_reviewed: 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025) Workshop: AI for Accelerated Materials Design
record.problems: The paper studies a single model architecture. The reconstruction-loss sweep is shown in figures without numerical values in the text, and it has no random-error comparison relevant to V3. The authors also state that stronger baselines are needed.
record.rows_left_out: No reported claim-relevant results were left out.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, failure on the same contexts, and persistence of error with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction harms model loss more than random errors of the same norm.
Whether the linear and nonlinear parts of the error differ in kind, and whether the nonlinear part resists further dictionary learning.
Whether steering or circuit analyses lose behaviour without the error term; the steering experiments never examine the error term.
Whether dark matter shrinks with different architectures or training objectives; only TopK SAEs were trained.

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source. The reader's 'tests/T2' classification and the V3 link on R1 are wrong. The loss sweep lacks the random-error comparator that defines V3, and it serves only to select hyperparameters. The SMILES reconstruction accuracy (Fig. S3) and steering-stability results are interpretability and fidelity results, not dark-matter measurements.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of SAE error is linearly predictable from the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether error persists with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction harms model loss more than random errors of the same size; no random-error comparison is reported.
Whether the linear component represents unlearned features and the nonlinear component is qualitatively distinct or resists further dictionary learning.
Whether SAE-feature-based analyses lose meaningful behavior when the error term is omitted.
Whether dark matter is chiefly a training artifact or shrinks with better architectures or end-to-end training.

rows.subject: SMI-TED
rows.operation_detail: Measured the change in SMI-TED loss when using SAE-reconstructed vectors instead of original vectors across the SAE sparsity and expansion sweep.
rows.measure: Delta loss, defined as SMI-TED loss on the reconstructed vector minus loss on the original vector
rows.baseline: SMI-TED loss on the original vector
rows.value: figure only; text states delta loss changes exponentially with sparsity and expansion factor has minimal impact at matched sparsity
rows.note: Measures the model-loss effect of SAE reconstruction, but the study does not compare it with random errors of the same size, so it cannot establish V3's stated comparison.
rows.check: Delta loss from substituting SAE reconstructions is a standard fidelity metric used for configuration selection. With no same-norm random-error baseline, it cannot bear on V3's pathological-error claim, so it should not be linked to V3. The value is figure-only; the text says only that the relationship with sparsity is exponential and that expansion factor has minimal impact.

tranche.reason: The study uses SAEs, but neither tests nor relies on a dark-matter finding. Reconstruction metrics select its own SAE configuration; using the underlying technique does not establish T4.

source_check.notes: Neither row measures V1–V6; retaining no version verdicts is appropriate. The 289M parameter count is explicitly stated in Section S1.4, although Figure 1 labels the model 298M.
